Aa

Macrons

Consonantal i

Consonantal u

Theme

Money, work & business

economy noun

careful use of money

also thrift, thriftiness, frugality, thrifty, economical

classical

Cic. Par. 49: quam magnum vectīgal sit parsimōnia
Cic. Off. 2.87: dīligentiā et parsimōniā

parsimōnia, parsimōniae f.

noun, first declension

thrift, careful spending

From parcō, spare; also written parcimōnia (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • frūgālitās, frūgālitātis f. — frugality, sober thrift

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Plin. Ep. 2.4.3: quod cessat ex reditū, frūgālitāte supplētur

    Thrift as a way of life; a thrifty, decent person is frūgī (indeclinable).

  • frūgī (indecl.) — thrifty, frugal; honest, useful (of a person)

    indeclinable adjective (an old dative of frūx); comparative frūgālior, superlative frūgālissimus · also used · classical · Cic. Deiot. 26: frūgī hominem dīcī nōn multum habet laudis in rēge (Lewis & Short s.v. frūx); Traupman 393

    The adjective for “thrifty”. Traupman also gives frūgālis, but Lewis & Short says it is classical only in the comparative and superlative (cf. Quint. 1.6.17); the positive is frūgī.

Examples

  • Ō dī immortālēs! nōn intellegunt hominēs, quam magnum vectīgal sit parsimōnia.

    Good heavens! People don’t understand what a great income thrift is.Cic. Par. 49

  • sed quod cessat ex reditū, frūgālitāte supplētur

    but whatever my income falls short by is made up by thriftPlin. Ep. 2.4.3

See also economy, income, economic.

SourcesLewis & Short: parsimonia · Lewis & Short: frugalitas · Lewis & Short: frugi
